sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Fast-Fashion Apparel and Footwear

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Income Tax Convention, signed 3 April 1996, as amended
Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Agreement, signed 12 March 1985, as amended
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union bilateral investment protection agreements, including the 1984 BLEU–China Investment Protection Agreement
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Agreement, signed 23 August 1951, as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant création d’un registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the application of the UBO register; implementing the EU Anti-Money Laundering Directive, in particular Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, register excerpt, or certificate of good standing of each corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent trade registry or companies registry in the foreign country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing country is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization through the Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg formation agent, lawyer, or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent authority in the country of origin of the corporate partner or authorised representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; notarial execution required if demanded by Luxembourg professional obligations

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each ultimate beneficial owner and authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary in the country of residence of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; certified translation into French, German, or Luxembourgish if the original is not in an official language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address, dated within the reservation window
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal authority, utility company, or bank in the country of residence of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where required; notarially certified copy accepted in certain non-contracting states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate ownership chart and UBO declaration of the corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate partner, company secretary, or the foreign beneficial-ownership register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the document is produced by a governmental registry; otherwise certified true copy signed before a notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorised signatories against the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC/SDN list, the Luxembourg national internal list of sanctioned persons, and the Luxembourg PEP database maintained by the Financial Intelligence Unit. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates. Ongoing transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting to the Cellule de Renseignement Financier are required under the Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, accessible via www.lbr.lu and www.guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be recorded in the Latin alphabet; the official filing language may be Luxembourgish, French, or German. Foreign-language names must be transliterated into Latin characters and, if necessary, certified translation must be provided. The registered name must begin with the commercial denomination and include the suffix 'SCSp' or 'société en commandite spéciale'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: any term suggesting regulated activity without prior ministerial approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be renewed by filing a fresh reservation through the Luxembourg Business Registers portal before expiry. If the Registrar rejects the proposed name, the applicant receives a written reason. The applicant may within one month file a reasoned administrative objection to the Registrar; if the objection is refused, recourse lies to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d’arrondissement) by way of a summary or declaratory action, with appeal to the Court of Appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted permissibility: the SCSp must maintain a registered office in Luxembourg, being a real physical address, not a mere P.O. Box or electronic mailbox. A third-party service provider’s office may be used as the registered address, but the place of effective central administration cannot automatically be relocated outside Luxembourg without risking tax-residency challenges. For an e-commerce retail SCSp, remote management is permissible provided core substance indicators, records, and decision-making functions remain verifiable in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: low, approximately 2% to 5% per annum for a non-regulated e-commerce SCSp. Unannounced physical inspections may nevertheless be carried out by the Luxembourg business register, tax authorities, or the AML monitoring authority where irregularities are suspected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and certificate of non-confusion
Apostille certification fee per foreign document (estimated for 3 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the originating state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Convention statutory fees / prevailing foreign registry fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign corporate and identity documents into French or German
Notarial authentication of partnership agreement and related powers of attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff for partnership formation instruments

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration filing fee and publication in the electronic register of companies and associations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO registration filing in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
Registered-office administration and corporate agent fee for first year
AML/KYC and PEP/sanctions screening compliance package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg AML compliance professional / notary office

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, Articles 99-1 to 99-15 establishing the Société en Commandite Spéciale; amended notably by the Law of 23 July 2016; supplementary RCS registration rules under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés de Luxembourg (RCS) administered by LBR under the supervision of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice; electronic filing via eJustice.public.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Immatriculation au RCS of the Société en Commandite Spéciale supported by the constitutive partnership agreement and the RCS registration declaration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp; the partnership agreement freely determines the subscribed capital and payment schedule. No escrow account is required by Luxembourg company law, but the bank account used for the first contribution must comply with normal AML/KYC verification.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the board of the initial corporate general partner approves the subscription of all partnership interests in the Société en Commandite Spéciale as stated in the register of partners, and confirms that every admitted partner and contribution is accepted. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the SCSp’s registered office is established at [registered address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and that [name] is appointed as gérant with sole day-to-day management authority. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the gérant is authorised to file the partnership agreement with the RCS Luxembourg, to open bank accounts, to apply for the business establishment authorisation, to register for VAT and to take all ancillary steps required for formation. All acts already done to date in this regard are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name reservation, partnership agreement drafting and registered office verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS via eJustice.public.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to eJustice.public.lu, submit a name availability query for the proposed SCSp name, confirm that the intended Luxembourg registered office is physically usable and legally available, and prepare the SCSp partnership agreement identifying the general partner, the limited partners, the capital contributions, profit shares, registered office and management powers.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of each partner
Proposed SCSp name and corporate purpose
Written confirmation of the registered office address
Draft SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS name search flags the proposed name as identical or confusingly similar, file a second-choice name through the same eJustice procedure; no substantive cure is required if the amendment is made before submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp partnership agreement and notarization if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public for authenticated form; alternatively the partners execute the act by private signed writing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure every partner or authorised representative signs the final partnership agreement; if the private-writing route is used, date and initial every page. Engage a Luxembourg notary when the RCS, bank or counterparty requires an authentic deed, and obtain corporate board approval where the general partner is a legal entity.
required_dossiers: Signed SCSp partnership agreement
Power of attorney for any representative
Corporate authorisation of the general partner if it is a corporate entity
Notarized act if the authenticated form is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or bank identifies conflicting clauses, execute a corrective amendment and re-sign; if a partner is disqualified or insolvent, replace the partner before the RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening the SCSp bank account and effecting subscribed contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Luxembourg credit institution selected by the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the signed partnership agreement and RCS name confirmation to the bank, complete the entity KYC and beneficial ownership forms, and open the account in the name of the SCSp. Credit the agreed initial contribution to the account and record it in the partners register. No minimum or escrow amount applies; the contribution schedule follows the partnership agreement.
required_dossiers: Draft or signed SCSp partnership agreement
RCS name reservation acknowledgment
Identity documents of signatories and beneficial owners
Bank KYC declaration and source-of-funds information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further AML evidence, provide notarized identity copies and a source-of-funds declaration; if the bank insists on an authenticated deed, revert to the notary in Step 2 before re-submitting KYC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and publication of incorporation formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS via eJustice.public.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the electronic RCS registration comprising the signed partnership agreement or authenticated deed, proof of registered office, manager consent and identity, and a completed registration declaration. Pay the filing fee online. Upon validation, the RCS issues the registration extract and trade register number; any mandatory RESA publication is processed by the registry.
required_dossiers: Executed SCSp partnership agreement
RCS registration declaration
Consent of the general partner or gérant to act
Proof of registered office address
Identity documents of partners and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for regularisation, respond electronically within 15 calendar days, attaching the missing annex or correcting the legal forms; if refusal persists, an appeal may be filed before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, commercial chamber.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, social security and business establishment licensing registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Direction générale des classes moyennes, Ministry of the Economy
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, obtain the Luxembourg national tax number and VAT number from the AEDT. If the SCSp will hire staff, register as an employer with the CCSS. For any Luxembourg physical office, depot or dispatch facility, submit a business establishment authorisation application to the Ministry of the Economy via MyGuichet.lu, attaching the floor plan, manager criminal record and owner consent.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
SCSp partnership agreement
Manager identity document and criminal record certificate
Complete VAT registration form
Business premises floor plan and owner authorisation
Employer registration form for CCSS if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business establishment authorisation is queried, provide supplementary security, floor-plan or professional qualification evidence to the SME Department within the notice period; for VAT issues, respond to the AEDT request and, if necessary, submit a formal request for a binding tax ruling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Direction générale des classes moyennes – SME and Business Establishment Authorisation Department; applications are submitted through MyGuichet.lu.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Authorisation (autorisation d'établissement) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011; no additional industrial factory licence applies to pure e-commerce apparel retailing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement – Luxembourg Environment Agency, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA for an online fashion retail operation without manufacturing; a declaration/notification before the Environment Agency is required only if a covered logistics depot exceeds 5,000 m² of floor area or if handling of dangerous goods creates waste streams above notification thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or solvent-based VOC emissions arise from e-commerce apparel dispatch; sanitary wastewater must comply with the municipal sewer ordinance and water-law quality requirements. Packaging waste must be recovered and reported under Luxembourg extended producer responsibility rules; hazardous waste, if any, must not exceed 1 tonne per site before a more extensive waste-management permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational clearance comprises a fire-safety visit by the Administration des services de secours / Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours, a structural load inspection certificate issued by a registered engineer for occupied storage floors, an electrical installation conformity check, and an occupational health and safety inspection by the Inspection du travail et des mines.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) is the Luxembourg indirect tax authority; direct income and corporate tax affairs are handled by Administration des contributions directes (ACD). The unified electronic portal is MyGuichet.lu / Guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity performing taxable activities in Luxembourg without a Luxembourg establishment must apply directly to the AEDT for a VAT identification number using the standard application form, supported by proof of identity, articles of incorporation, confirmation of foreign VAT registration, and evidence of the taxable activity. If required, a Luxembourg fiscal representative must be appointed. Luxembourg resident entities receive a national business number at RCS registration and obtain a separate VAT number through the AEDT upon filing the application after registration or before commencing taxable operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is disregarded as a separate taxpayer for Luxembourg direct tax purposes; there is no general check-the-box-type election. Tax transparency is the default statutory classification. For VAT purposes, the SCSp is treated as a separate taxable person. Advance tax rulings confirming transparency are available through the Luxembourg tax administration. Hybrid mismatch rules in Luxembourg domestic legislation may recharacterise a transparent partnership if a foreign jurisdiction treats the same SCSp as taxable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (Luxembourg Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The Luxembourg domestic VAT registration threshold is EUR 35,000 of annual taxable turnover. For intra-EU distance sales of goods and B2C e-services, the mandatory VAT registration threshold for non-resident EU suppliers is EUR 10,000 of annual cross-border turnover unless the supplier elects to charge local VAT via the One-Stop Shop (OSS).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based pre-clearance of e-invoices. Electronic invoicing is required for suppliers to the Luxembourg public sector using the PEPPOL format. Private B2B and B2C e-invoices must satisfy VAT invoice content and archiving requirements but are not subject to mandatory clearance. OSS digital filings are made via the national OSS portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported or dispatched to any non-EU destination if the exporter retains documentary evidence that the goods left the EU. Supply must be made to a customer with a permanent business destination outside the EU, and title must pass; e-commerce parcels shipped directly to non-EU consumers qualify if the seller holds proof of export and transport. Intra-EU B2C e-commerce sales are not zero-rated and are instead taxable in the destination member state via OSS. Offshore services relating to the fast-fashion retail business are generally outside scope unless physically used in Luxembourg.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document or electronic ECS declaration)
Commercial Invoice assigned to the first non-EU buyer
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from Luxembourg/EU
Packing List and proof of consignment matching the customs declaration
Third-country customs entry documentation or electronic transport tracking record
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT confirmation of payment from the non-EU buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may perform retrospective audits within the standard five-year assessment window and assess under-declared VAT at 17% plus monthly interest of 0.6%. Where zero-rating is claimed without substantiating export documentation, the supply is recharacterised as a domestic taxable supply, resulting in full VAT liability, input credit disallowance, administrative fines up to EUR 10,000, and in cases of deliberate fraud, criminal penalties including imprisonment up to five years and fines of up to EUR 50,000. Proceeds not repatriated within 180 days of export invoice maturity are subject to heightened anti-abuse scrutiny and may trigger retroactive clawback of export deductions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) operating within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank (ECB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises Luxembourg banks, payment institutions, and electronic money institutions, while BCL collects balance-of-payments (BoP) statistical data via resident credit institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Euro is fully convertible and is the sole legal tender of Luxembourg. Luxembourg applies no exchange-control regime; unrestricted free movement of capital and payments is guaranteed under Article 63 TFEU and the EU Capital Movements Directive (88/361/EEC). Both current-account flows (e-commerce sales proceeds, trade disbursements) and capital-account flows (equity contributions, partner loans, profit distributions, liquidation surplus) are permitted without prior authorization, and there are no profit-remittance hurdles for a non-resident-owned SCSp. The only compliance friction is BoP statistical reporting: every cross-border transaction, including SEPA and SEPA Instant transfers, must carry a BCL purpose code captured by the servicing bank, with third-country transactions reported by the bank on a monthly basis.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg and the Eurozone impose no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandated repatriation period, and no minimum conversion ratio for foreign-currency receipts. The SCSp may retain USD, GBP, and CNY e-commerce revenue in domestic multi-currency sub-accounts or in offshore settlement accounts and convert only as dictated by operational cash-flow needs.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR treasury current account) with multi-currency sub-accounts (USD, GBP, CNY) and optional Capital Escrow Account for partner injections

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE, Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR settlement) with SEPA Direct Debit collection and dedicated e-commerce merchant settlement sub-account
Operational Account with SWIFT GPI access, cash-pooling overlay, and Capital Escrow sub-account for loan drawdowns
Operational Account (dual EUR/USD) with commercial letter of credit and trade-finance documentary collection facilities
Operational Account (EUR) with cross-border cash management and electronic banking platform
Operational Account (EUR) with e-banking and SEPA DD collection capabilities
Private-banking multi-asset account, better suited to capital escrow and wealth-linked treasury than high-volume e-commerce operations

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-to-high as a secondary collection and settlement rail; Low as the sole treasury account. Luxembourg-licensed entities operating under PSD2, such as PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. & Cie S.C.A. and Six Payment Services Luxembourg, are acceptable for merchant settlement and BNPL reconciliation. EU/EEA payment institutions and EMIs may passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 without a branch, and Luxembourg banks will normally accept settlement flows from passported EMIs. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Currenxie, Wise Business, Multitude) may be used only for foreign-currency supplier payouts and never as the main treasury repository, because an unlicensed or non-passported EMI arrangement exposes the SCSp to CSSF regulatory scrutiny and degrades its Low_Risk_Standard AML classification. Contractual structuring must ensure that end-of-day balances are swept to a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution before onward disbursement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) does not statutorily mandate face-to-face identity verification where a robust remote identification mechanism is applied; however, in practice, Tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one onboarding interview for an SCSp. This interview may be conducted physically at the bank's premises in Luxembourg City or by bank-grade video conference supplemented by a qualified electronic signature (eIDAS or LuxTrust certificate). Remote account opening is generally accepted for a low-risk, non-resident-owned commercial SCSp where: (i) all signatories and ultimate beneficial owners pass video identification, (ii) the initial funds originate from regulated banking accounts, and (iii) the general partner's management has a verifiable professional track record. After the first account opening, treasury operations are fully remote. If any limited partner is resident in a FATF high-risk third country or the injection exceeds EUR 250,000, a physical meeting with the beneficial owner or a Luxembourg-based authorized representative (mandataire) becomes effectively mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The SCSp lacks legal personality and the bank must map the general partner, its directors, and every beneficial owner (typically limited partners holding 25% or more) before account activation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the partnership agreement (contrat de société) as filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS); RCS extract not older than three months; RBE beneficial-owner registration confirmation; passports and proof of address of each UBO; general-partner board resolution appointing account signatories; signed UBO declaration and ownership chart; source-of-wealth statement; and 12-month bank statements of the funding entity or individual for the initial capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border card and BNPL settlement flows from Shopify Payments and Klarna create chargeback and refund noise that can be misread as third-party payment processing or unlicensed money service activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant acquirer agreements; 12-month settlement and chargeback reports showing a chargeback ratio below 1%; PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation of compliance; documented refund policy and customer-service workflow; Shopify store ownership and platform verification certificate; and a monthly reconciliation of gross receipts to Luxembourg VAT returns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound MT103 disbursements to garment suppliers in Bangladesh, Vietnam, China, and Turkey, which are corridors subject to elevated correspondent-bank scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-supplier KYC file comprising trade registry certificate, business license extract, and director passport; signed purchase orders and pro-forma invoices; shipping documents (bill of lading, airway bill, CMR); customs declarations; supplier bank account confirmation letter; and a documented trade-chain narrative evidencing genuine garment procurement and retail distribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partner loan funding from non-resident individual investors lacking a commercially justified purpose and arms'-length documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed partner loan agreements with market-rate interest and a defined repayment schedule; source-of-funds bank statements and tax records of the lenders; general-partner capital-call resolution; projected cash-flow statement demonstrating the operational need; and confirmation that the loan is booked as partner debt consistent with the SCSp's tax-transparent classification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All capital injections must be routed for the account of the SCSp and executed by SWIFT MT103, or SEPA Credit Transfer where the remitter holds EUR, to the Luxembourg concentration account at a BCL-reporting bank. The transfer must reference the SCSp name, the general partner, and a unique injection reference (e.g., SCSP-CAP-001). The bank will assign a BoP purpose code from the code families defined under Regulation (EU) No 184/2005, typically one covering direct or other investment equity and loans; the servicer must confirm the exact code at onboarding. For each injection the bank file must contain: (i) a signed capital-call or loan-drawdown notice; (ii) the relevant partnership agreement or resolution; (iii) UBO confirmation for the funding limited partner; and (iv) proof of origin of funds for transactions above EUR 100,000. Where the injection originates from a jurisdiction with outbound capital controls, such as China's SAFE or India's FEMA, the remitting partner must obtain the home-country outbound investment approval before transfer, and a copy must be deposited with the Luxembourg bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EU supplier payments are cleared via SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) through EBA STEP2 or TIPS with near-real-time settlement. Non-EU suppliers are paid by SWIFT MT103 GPI in the invoice currency (EUR, USD, or GBP) with full structured remittance advice and a BoP trade purpose code. For large wholesale purchase orders above EUR 250,000, the SCSp should issue an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit via the account bank's trade desk using MT700/MT707 messages, or a documentary collection (cash against documents) for established suppliers. Supplier advances are prohibited unless covered by a standby LC or a contractual trade-finance facility. Refunds and chargebacks related to Klarna BNPL, Shopify Payments, and card acquirers must be funded from the EUR settlement account and executed through the respective acquirer or BNPL refund APIs, with daily reconciliation against the order-management system to preserve the audit trail and the Low_Risk_Standard AML profile.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX agreements for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNY executed through the Luxembourg clearing bank's FX desk for immediate trade settlements
Plain-vanilla FX forwards with tenors up to 12 months, settled on a deliverable basis within the Eurozone for hedging forecast supplier costs and cross-border revenue repatriation
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) settled in EUR, permitted only for non-convertible or restricted currencies such as offshore CNY (CNH), under an ISDA or master agreement with the account bank
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (XCCY) under an ISDA/CSA with the Luxembourg counterparty for aligning EUR-denominated partner loan funding with USD or GBP revenue streams
FX options and zero-cost collars for low-risk hedging of treasury flows, documented within the SCSp's treasury policy and designated for hedge accounting under IFRS 9 where applicable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (confirmation annuelle RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), filed electronically via MyGuichet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due every year within one month of the RBE annual recall notice, which is issued one month before the anniversary of the SCSp's initial RBE registration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of €500 to €1,250 per missed or inaccurate confirmation; intentional non-compliance triggers criminal sanctions for the gérant, with fines up to €125,000 and/or up to six months' imprisonment, and fines up to €1,250,000 for legal entities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS data confirmation statement (confirmation annuelle des données du Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS, filed electronically via MyGuichet
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the RCS registration anniversary; LBR sends an electronic reminder approximately one month before that date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Repeated non-confirmation triggers formal LBR reminders, referral to the District Public Prosecutor, court-ordered compliance under a daily coercive fine (astreinte), and ultimately administrative strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SCSp annual declaration of exemption from publication of annual accounts under Article 75-3 of the amended Law of 10 August 1915, where all general and limited partners are legal entities or regulated undertakings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS, with publication in RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the statutory annual accounts filing deadline, in practice no later than seven months after the end of the financial year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The publication exemption lapses and the RCS will require the full annual accounts to be filed and made public at the SCSp's expense; a false declaration exposes the gérant to criminal sanctions and civil liability toward the limited partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts of the SCSp (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes) and, where applicable, the statutory audit report, deposited with the RCS and published in RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the end of the financial year (for a calendar-year SCSp: by 31 July of the following year).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The RCS issues a formal notice after default; if the accounts remain unfiled, the Public Prosecutor or any interested party may petition the District Court for a filing order with a daily astreinte. Persistent default can lead to strike-off and personal liability of the gérant for third-party damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax return (déclaration de l'impôt commercial communal - ICC) covering the e-commerce retail activity of the fast-fashion apparel business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Bureau d'imposition; copy to the municipal tax office of the registered office commune
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December of the year following the tax year, unless a filing extension is granted by the competent ACD bureau.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on the ICC due plus monthly default interest; wilful or repeated default may lead to ex-officio assessment, a 20% penalty, and criminal fines against the gérant.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit (révision légale) is mandatory for the SCSp when at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded at the balance-sheet date: balance sheet total above €4.4 million; net turnover above €8.8 million; average of more than 50 full-time equivalent employees during the financial year. A fast-fashion e-commerce SCSp in the ISIC 4791 retail scope normally falls below these thresholds in its early years and is therefore audit-exempt unless the partnership agreement or a partner validly requires an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified by the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); EU-endorsed IFRS may alternatively be adopted for statutory purposes. The SCSp's income and expenses follow the partnership agreement while remaining subject to Luxembourg accounting and transparency rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must annually confirm through the RBE online portal that the recorded beneficial ownership information is accurate and complete; the confirmation is due within one month after the annual recall email issued by LBR. Every transfer of partnership interests during the year, including equity changes linked to growth financing of the e-commerce venture, must be reported to the RBE within one month of the transfer. The annual confirmation serves as the final reconciliation point for the updated ownership chain up to natural persons holding more than 25% or otherwise exercising control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Partners) - individual and legal entity holdings
Register of General Partners (Commandités) and Managers (Gérants)
Minute Book (registre des décisions) of partner and manager resolutions
Register of partnership interest transfers, pledges and usufructs

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200 - US$2,900 per year for professional domiciliation and corporate agent services in Luxembourg City for an SCSp structure
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$6,000 - US$15,000 for a full statutory audit by an accredited réviseur d'entreprises agréé for a small-to-mid-market retail entity; US$3,500 - US$7,000 for a voluntary review engagement when the SCSp remains below the audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% for FY2024; 18% for FY2025 onward; plus 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax (Luxembourg City base rate 6.75%) producing aggregate burden of 24.94% (FY2024) and 26.01% (FY2025) for corporate partners. The SCSp itself, as a fiscally transparent partnership, is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is tax-transparent: profits flow through to partners. Qualifying corporate partners benefit from the 100% participation exemption on dividends and capital gains (10% holding, 12-month holding, and substance conditions); modified nexus IP regime exempts 80% of qualifying net IP income; domestic loss offset is unlimited in time but capped at EUR 17,280,000 per tax year (excess offset restricted to 50%); no notional interest deduction currently available for SCSp.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 851 (Corporate Income Tax and Municipal Business Tax return) with partnership annex; filed electronically through the e-CDF portal (MyGuichet.lu); the SCSp must also register with the Luxembourg indirect tax and social security authorities where e-commerce activity creates a Luxembourg permanent establishment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly prepayments of corporate income tax and municipal business tax for entities with taxable Luxembourg presence.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 May of the year following the tax year; automatic administrative extension to 31 December for e-CDF electronic filings; paper filings require a written extension request (standard 3-month extension).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification and status of the taxable person: name, Luxembourg trade register number, national tax number, registered office, place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must disclose their foreign tax residence, Luxembourg PE registration, and the identity of the Luxembourg fiscal agent; disregard funds not attributable to the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit per statutory financial statements before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Luxembourg-source e-commerce income allocable to the SCSp/PE under Article 157 LIR; remote sales with no Luxembourg PE remain outside the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividend income and capital gains qualifying for the participation exemption (requires 10% minimum shareholding and 12-month holding period).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only if the non-resident partner satisfies the crystallized holding conditions and the Luxembourg substance requirements; retain share registers and bank evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses brought forward from prior years and losses utilised in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only losses legally borne by the same partner or PE; transparent pass-through preserves loss history of the partner; losses above EUR 17,280,000 current-year offset are limited to 50% of the excess.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before allowances allocated to municipal business tax (communal trade tax).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents: leave nil unless a Luxembourg PE exists; for existing PEs, apportion direct e-commerce logistics, inventory and fulfilment functions against the Luxembourg profit base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: warning, forced assessment, and fine up to EUR 750 per return; late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month; negligence surcharge on under-declaration 10%; intentional evasion surcharge 50%; tax fraud triggers criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (up to 10 years in aggravated cases).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for 12 months and meeting substance conditions; SCSp distributions are generally outside Luxembourg dividend WHT where the partnership is transparent and the distribution is a return of capital or profit share.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Beneficial owner must submit a valid Luxembourg Tax Administration (AED) residence certificate (Form 6TR) and a declaration of beneficial ownership to the paying agent before the payment date to apply the treaty rate at source. For refunds, the claimant files a refund request within 3 years of the dividend payment with the AED, attaching the TRC, audited financial statements, share register, and proof of withholding; EU companies may use the simplified Parent-Subsidiary Directive zero-rate procedure on prior approval.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest is 0%; EU Interest and Royalties Directive also applies at 0%; Luxembourg DTAs generally allocate royalties and interest to the beneficial owner's state of residence at 0% or provide full exemption in Luxembourg.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 150,000: annual related-party transactions exceeding this threshold trigger the duty to prepare, maintain, and produce on request contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File); consolidated groups with revenues of EUR 750 million or more must also prepare a Master File and CbC Report.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations but imposes substance requirements through ATAD general anti-abuse rules, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive anti-abuse clause, PE attribution rules, and administrative circulars on holding companies. A fast-fashion e-commerce SCSp claiming tax benefits must demonstrate real local activity: strategic management decisions in Luxembourg, employees, office premises, e-commerce platform oversight, inventory and fulfilment control, bank accounts, and compliance records; absence of substance enables recharacterization of the SCSp as a foreign-managed shell and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of e-commerce sales revenue, fabrication of marketing and logistics costs, off-book cash distributions to hidden beneficial owners, or submission of knowingly false Form 851 declarations for the SCSp.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Evasion surcharge of 50% of evaded tax plus monthly late interest of 0.6%; criminal tax fraud penalties up to EUR 250,000 fine and 1-5 years imprisonment, extended to 10 years with aggravating circumstances; forced tax assessment and seizure of bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and fines where they controlled the filing and concealed facts; courts may impose travel bans, asset freezes, and disqualification orders, with imprisonment up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp as a letterbox e-commerce principal: all fast-fashion procurement, logistics, customer service, and platform functions performed abroad, no Luxembourg employees or local management, transactions structured solely to capture Luxembourg treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ATAD GAAR recharacterization of the arrangement, denial of Luxembourg treaty and Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefits, reallocation of profits to the foreign beneficial owner's jurisdiction, reassessment with penalties of 10%-50% of additional tax, and possible compulsory liquidation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal civil liability for re-assessed taxes, deregistration of the entity, travel restrictions pending investigation, and personal fines for participating in artificial designs.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's length transactions: inflated royalty payments to related IP companies, overpriced sourcing fees from foreign affiliates, excessive management charges, and allocation of all residual e-commerce profit to low-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Arm's length primary adjustment, secondary recharacterization of payments as constructive dividends or equity contributions, monthly interest at 0.6%, penalty of 10%-50% of the reassessed tax, and application of CFC rules to redirect passive income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation face personal civil restitution, joint and several liability for the group companies' tax debts, and criminal liability for falsification of accounting records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing proceeds from counterfeit or prohibited fast-fashion sales, obscuring the ultimate beneficial owner through SCSp partnership layers, invoice laundering through shell bank accounts, or facilitating fraudulent BNPL payment schemes linked to the apparel e-commerce platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg AML law imposes imprisonment of 5-10 years (aggravated up to 10 years), fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or five times the value of laundered assets, confiscation of bank accounts and goods, forced liquidation, and publication of sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil is pierced in money laundering cases: directors, officers, and the general partner incur joint restitution obligations, travel bans, and freezing orders; imprisonment applies to individuals knowingly directing the laundering scheme.
